clue.text: Animals are increasing, we hear, in swampy areas

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the phrase before it is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: if donkeys are growing in number there are more asses

explanation.surface: A remark that the beasts multiply as you hear it said, out in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals the sound: MORE ASSES, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or marsh, so the plural names boggy, waterlogged ground.

clue.text: Magician's bird

definitions.meaning: the wizard of the Arthurian legends

explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is King Arthur's wizard and also a small falcon.

clue.text: Early activity in West End to acquire freehold land

indicators.note: to acquire means the jumbled word takes another letter inside it
activity suggests the letters of early are set busily moving into a new order
End points to the final letter of west

explanation.surface: Morning business in London's theatreland buys up property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activity' rearranges EARLY to REALY; 'to acquire' puts T, the end of 'West', inside it. 'West End' looks like London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is real estate, property in land and buildings.

clue.text: Pack-horse has rump set out of joint

indicators.note: out of joint means dislocated, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A carrying horse has dislocated its hindquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sumpter is an old word for a beast carrying baggage.

clue.text: Rent reduced by a pound, so relax

indicators.note: reduced by says the letter for a pound is subtracted from the rental word

parts.note: a lease is a rental agreement, so rent
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The rent has come down a pound, so you can unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen up or take it easy is to relax.

clue.text: I am taking a long time forming concepts

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
ages means a long time, as in 'I waited for ages'

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they are slow at coming up with ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental pictures or ideas formed in the mind are concepts.

clue.text: Grim end to half-hearted song leads to feverish complaint

indicators.note: end to points to the final letter of grim
hearted indicates the central letters of the word half

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: A gloomy finish to a weak ballad brings on a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' is split: 'hearted' takes the heart of 'half', AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease marked by recurring fevers.

clue.text: Wins assistance when opposed

parts.note: gains means wins
aid means help, assistance

explanation.surface: Getting help when facing opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsaid means contradicted, spoken against.

clue.text: No encore to this rendering!

parts.note: a performance after which nothing more follows because it is the singer's final one

explanation.definitionFit: A swan-song is a farewell performance, the last thing anyone will hear.

clue.text: Have greatest number of offspring after all

definitions.meaning: to ... children is to raise the largest brood
coming behind everything else, at the very back

explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means last of all, positioned behind every other one.

clue.text: Live round the artillery put into her

indicators.note: round suggests the letters of live are turned about into a new order

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Instructions to go and live near the guns placed in a woman's keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like a verb but is the anagram fodder; 'put into' is only a link to the definition, a pronoun standing for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvira is a woman's given name, so a female, referred to as her.

clue.text: Court disaster, working landing up in the soup

indicators.note: disaster suggests the letters of court are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: on means working, as in 'the machine is on'

explanation.surface: Courting disaster while busy, someone ends up in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges COURT to CROUT. 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A crouton is a cube of fried bread dropped into soup.

clue.text: At home, an infant needs love, entirely

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a tot is a small child
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A baby at home needs affection completely.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, completely or altogether.

clue.text: Supporters with guns hemming in the others

indicators.note: hemming in means surrounding, so the word for guns goes around the word for the others

parts.note: arms are weapons, guns
the rest means the others, the remainder

explanation.surface: Armed backers surround everybody else.
explanation.definitionFit: Armrests support a seated person's arms, so they are literal supports.

clue.text: The dignitaries associated with crooks

parts.note: senior clergy carry a crook-shaped staff, rather than consorting with criminals

explanation.definitionFit: Bishops carry a crozier, a shepherd's crook, as a symbol of office.

clue.text: Italian court throwing out this speech-making process

indicators.note: throwing out suggests the letters of the two words are flung about and land in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An Italian judge dismissing a case about oratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear forming of spoken sounds is how speech is produced, the process of enunciating words.

clue.text: May bless reformed flock

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A blessing for a church congregation that has been reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock is a gathered congregation, a group assembled together.

clue.text: Song made over gear crazy boy put on

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the word for crazy above the word for gear
put on means the boy's name is attached below the rest

parts.note: mad means crazy
rig means gear, equipment
Al is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A tune composed about a crazy boy dressing up in gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices, usually unaccompanied.

clue.text: Aiming weapon at owl on flat opposite?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Aiming weapon at owl on flat opposite?' has no enumeration and no definition of a marksman; SHARP (flat opposite) + HOOTER (owl) leaves the S unaccounted, so the clue appears cut short in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Aiming weapon at owl on flat opposite?

clue.text: Cloth limit, intake of English and other church members

indicators.note: intake of means the boundary word takes the letters inside it

parts.note: a pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'
RC is Roman Catholic, a church other than the English one

explanation.surface: A limit on cloth, and an influx of English and other churchgoers.
explanation.definitionFit: Percale is a closely woven cotton fabric used for bed linen.

clue.text: Rising fury over rate change in Africa

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
rising in a down clue means the word for fury is read upwards

parts.note: ire means anger, fury

indicators.note: change tells the solver to rearrange the letters of rate

explanation.surface: Anger grows over a change in exchange rates somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns IRE to ERI; 'change' rearranges RATE to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa, so a place there.

clue.text: Judge indisposed to have another pint?

parts.note: a referee judges a match, shortened to ref
ill means unwell, indisposed

explanation.surface: A sick referee wants a second drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass again is to take another drink.

clue.text: Hound or hound's prey

definitions.meaning: the striped animal hunted by dogs

explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester; the badger is also an animal dogs were used to hunt.

clue.text: Jewellery used medicinally?

parts.note: the word names pendant earrings and also liquid medicine dripped into the ear, so jewellery that is medicine

explanation.definitionFit: Ear-drops are both drop earrings and medicated liquid for the ear.

clue.text: Screening last word I caught on return trip

indicators.note: on return trip tells the solver the whole string is to be read going back the other way

parts.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Getting the final say on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return trip' reverses the whole run AMEN + I + C into CINEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture house is where films are given a screening, so the venue stands for showing films.

clue.text: Point to litter-holder-it's an eyesore

indicators.note: to means the compass point is attached after the pen

parts.note: a sty is a pen holding a litter of piglets
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Pointing to the pigpen as an ugly sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Requiring money to get something to eat in the pub?

indicators.note: in places the food inside the word for the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is something to eat

explanation.surface: Asking for cash to buy a bar snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a beggar is one requiring money, so read the phrase as describing such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant asks others for cash because they are in need of it.

clue.text: Expressing surprise at the beginning

definitions.meaning: jumping or flinching suddenly when shocked
commencing, setting off at the outset

explanation.definitionFit: Starting means both giving a sudden jump of surprise and beginning.

clue.text: The egg, for example, yokel's thrown at old copper

indicators.note: thrown suggests the letters of the country bumpkin are knocked into disorder

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter
D was the abbreviation for the old British penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin hurls an egg at a policeman of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the coin: D was the pre-decimal British penny. The definition is a quirky example of something with a yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg is the standard example of something containing a yellow centre.

clue.text: Tradesman who passes on the account?

definitions.meaning: a shopkeeper selling goods to the public
one who retails a story tells it again, passing on the tale

explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper sells goods; to retail is also to recount a story, so one who retells it.
